parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity, a national hate-crime statute covering gender identity and functioning courts that have blocked several orders keep this well above the severe-risk tier. But the combined regime carries several documented traveller-facing exposures: a national entry regime in which sex-marker discrepancies trigger refusal and evidence demands, with a possible permanent fraud-based ineligibility finding, and foreign governments have issued trans-specific advisories; a state prison system that now bars hormones with no taper, on top of documented national custody practices (hair-cutting, hormone removal, reported abuse in immigration detention). Facility bans are not documented for this division itself, and no trans-specific violence incident in this state is recorded. A hostile legislature, surgical-requirement document rules and no state gender-identity non-discrimination law leave the remedy thin, placing it just below the elevated band's midpoint.

entry_documents.exposure: National inspection/visa cable directs refusal and further evidence where documents suggest a sex discrepancy; a material-misrepresentation finding can yield lifetime ineligibility. Athlete entry ban. Advisories from at least eight governments.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding is never automatic and requires four elements; waivers exist; litigation ongoing.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-issued foreign passports are unaffected by the domestic marker rules, but inspection-stage doubt is resolved by national officers whose refusal strands the traveller.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State law (HB 2009, eff. 2 July 2026) bars hormones/surgery for inmates with no taper; national corrections model removes hormones and imposes psychiatric substitution; immigration custody records forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no state custody protocol protecting trans detainees is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border or street incident escalating to detention routes the traveller into a custody system documented as harmful.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National-state patchwork bans facility use by gender identity, with four states criminalising it and one documented arrest and men's-ward hold; this division's own facility rule is not stated in the division evidence.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Two municipal sanctuary ordinances; no statewide facility protection documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exposure here would arise from local policy or private venue practice rather than a documented state statute.

care_services.exposure: SAFE Act bars minors' hormones/blockers and all surgery, bars Medicaid coverage at any age, exposes providers to licence loss and suits; a tipline invites reports.
care_services.protection: Minors already in treatment may continue; transition care not the object of a visitor's trip.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor finds no lawful local care option; adult visitor emergency care is not documented as denied.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for prioritised neutralisation; a reward memorandum invokes 'radical gender ideology'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; no documented prosecution of trans individuals under these texts.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises the temperature around visible advocacy and could colour police framing of a complainant, but no enforcement against travellers is recorded.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban upheld on appeal; ballot initiative seeks permanence; national order directs investigation of schools and prosecution of teachers using a minor's preferred name.
minors_guardians.protection: Sunset in 2027; grandfathering of existing patients; litigation history.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces a state that treats the minor's social transition as harm; no custody or documentation protection for the family is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated trans-specific violence incident in this division is recorded; hostile public opinion (66% support birth-sex document rules) and no state non-discrimination law.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute expressly covers gender identity; national hate-crime statute applies; two sanctuary cities.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists on paper through hate-crime law, but absent non-discrimination coverage and with adversarial official rhetoric, victims' willingness to report is uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Document rules require surgical certification with no remaining workaround; licence-marker change reverted to surgery or court order after an unexplained incident.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ongoing national litigation, injunctions against several orders, legal-aid FAQ, sanctuary ordinances.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court relief has been partial and adverse at state level, so the traveller cannot rely on pending challenges at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Kestrelia denies entry but explicitly bars detention for marker discrepancies and imposes no lasting immigration consequence. This dossier is worse: refusal can be paired with a permanent fraud-based ineligibility finding and evidence demands, and custody harm is documented rather than excluded.

The hostel anchor has anti-discrimination rules (weakly enforced), no detention, and only service-level friction. This dossier has heavier state-driven exposures (custody hormone denial, entry refusal machinery) but also a genuine hate-crime statute and no documented facilities ban, placing it near or slightly below that level.

The Vaelen extortion case involves coercive custody, threatened imprisonment for identity misrepresentation and no protective institutions. Here there is no trans-specific offence and courts sometimes intervene, but documented custody practices and entry-refusal rules share its humiliation-and-detention character, so this dossier sits materially higher.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is layered. The border is the first filter: national inspection rules treat a sex discrepancy as grounds for refusal and possible lifetime inadmissibility, and allied governments have flagged the risk. Once inside, everyday life in this division is not criminalised, but institutions are hostile: care for minors is banned, prison hormones are cut without taper, documents require surgical proof, and civil-rights law omits gender identity, while the national government frames pro-trans advocacy as a security concern. Protections that do operate are juridical, not administrative: a gender-identity hate-crime statute, litigation that has stalled parts of the executive programme, and municipal sanctuary ordinances. A visitor who is outed therefore faces real refusal, service and custody exposure with recourse that is partial and contested.
